text.p: Following are the main stories in Monday's Malaysian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Two senior United Malays National Organisation (UMNO) leaders today said party leaders drawn into cases that could tarnish the image and reputation of the party should consider relinquishing their posts.
- The police and the immigration department are the Home Ministry's top two government agencies where corruption occurs frequently, its Deputy Minister Megat Junid Megat Ayob said today.
- The former head of UMNO's women's group Rafidah Aziz today welcomed the party's supreme council decision to investigate the accounts of the movement.
- The Home Ministry will appoint special "spies" in the police and immigration departments, which are among government departments identified as being largely involved in corruption.
- Outgoing Selangor Chief Minister Muhammad Muhammad Taib has urged all party members to give their full support to his successor.
- Once corporatised, Bank Simpanan Nasional aims to merge its commercial banking arm with at least three other banks to create a banking giant that will rival Malayan Banking Bhd.

- In emerging as the world's most dynamic exporter between 1990 and 1996 with an average growth of 18 percent based on U.S. dollar terms, Malaysia was ranked the 12th largest exporter and 11th largest importer last year.
- Kumpulan Guthrie Bhd is exploring the possibility of acquiring firms that are engaged in activities related to those of the Malaysian conglomerate.
